keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Shu Han row begins in 224, but Liu Bei held land from 209 ('Zhou Yu captures Jiangling. Liu Bei takes the Xiang River commanderies'). The extent is my reading of 'Xiang River commanderies' as Hunan; the sibling liu-biao dossier names Nan, Lingling and Wuling instead. Fix fx-31 (F168): kept. The Liu Bei page (opened 2026-11-01) has Liu Bei 'capture the four commanderies in southern Jing Province': 'Changsha led by Han Xuan, Lingling led by Liu Du, Guiyang led by Zhao Fan and Wuling led by Jin Xuan' (undated there; the Shu Han page dates the Xiang River commanderies to 209), so all of Hunan is Liu Bei's in 209-213. The Jing Province page's split 'Jiangxia, Guiyang and Changsha to Sun Quan' (winter 208/209) is the sibling liu-biao dossier's reading and contradicts the Liu Bei page; this dossier's own 215 partition (ledger 5) is where Changsha and Guiyang pass to Wu. Handoff: liu-biao successor land for eastern-wu (all Hunan) is too wide.

notes:
STATE START. Cliopatria's Shu Han row is 224-262. The state was proclaimed in May 221 (infobox) and Liu Bei took Yi Province in 214 (Three Kingdoms page); the sibling dossiers (liu-biao, liu-zhang) already name shu-han as their successor from 209 and 214, so this dossier starts at 209 with Liu Bei's Xiang River commanderies, so that the land does not fall out of the map in 209-223. If the compiler prefers a 221 start, 209-220 should be drawn as Liu Bei's regime under another name.
NEW KEYFRAMES. 209-213 (Hunan), 214, 215-218 (Yi plus the Xiang commanderies west of the river), 219-224 (Yi plus Hanzhong). Cliopatria's 224 shape includes Nanzhong; the page dates the expedition to 225, so the shape holds from 225.
DISAGREEMENTS. (1) The Jing commanderies: this dossier follows the Three Kingdoms page (Liu Bei takes the Xiang River commanderies; Zhou Yu takes Jiangling, 209; Xiang border 215); the sibling liu-biao dossier, from the Jing Province page not opened here, gives Nan, Lingling and Wuling to Liu Bei and Changsha, Guiyang and Jiangxia to Sun Quan in 209. (2) Xiaoting: 221 (Three Kingdoms) or 222 (Shu Han page).
GAPS (page silent). The year Wudu and Yinping were taken from Wei (the Shu Han page lists them as 'conquered from Wei' without a year); the extent of the Nanzhong revolt before 225; Liu Bei's seat in 209-213; the later Jiang Wei expeditions (247-262), not on the pages opened. No infobox area exists on the Shu Han page.
BUDGET. Four pages opened (budget 1-2), three of them shared with the cao-wei, cao-cao and eastern-wu dossiers of the same batch.
COUNTERPARTS WITHOUT A DOSSIER. 'Nanzhong rebels' (the tribal chiefs and Yong Kai's group, 222-225) have none; the pages opened do not name them.
